summary: Verified the X-style Profile avatar-vs-cover-banner stacking fix on /profile (web only, frontend-only per request). The avatar wrapper now has position:relative + z-index:10 and sits ON TOP of the cover banner. Confirmed in both Dark and Light themes with screenshots and a programmatic elementFromPoint check at the overlap region (returned the avatar , not the banner div). Header (name, @handle, OFFICIAL badge, bio, inline counts), Edit profile + Invite pill actions, and all profile tabs (Posts/Reels/Videos/Blogs) render and switch content correctly. BUG FIX = PASS.
critical_code_review_comments: Minor: The review_request mentions follow-list stat testIDs as 'profile-stat-followers / profile-stat-following', but Profile.jsx actually uses 'profile-followers-stat' / 'profile-following-stat' (lines 240-241). Not a bug — just a naming note for future test prompts.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Profile avatar overlap fix verified. Measured: banner bottom y=201, avatar top y=137 (64px overlap into banner). avatarWrap computed style = position:relative, z-index:10. elementFromPoint at the overlap zone returns the avatar IMG (not the banner div), proving the avatar paints on top. Both Dark and Light theme screenshots show the avatar fully visible with the ring-4 ring-card border creating the X-style cutout. No regressions on tabs or header content.
rca of the issue: Original bug: cover banner div (position: relative) created a stacking context that painted above subsequent static siblings, clipping the avatar that was pulled up via negative margin. Fix: added 'relative z-10' to the avatar wrapper, giving it its own positioned stacking so it renders above the banner. Verified via computed styles and elementFromPoint hit-testing.
